findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State what 'measurably beats' means for the verdict (e.g. a directional threshold such as >=X% overlap-rate reduction OR >=1 fewer attempt-to-clean-close on the majority of tickets), acknowledging the small-n PoC caveat.
evidence: 'Verdict comment: does the exclusion list measurably beat plain cache-seeded resume?'
No stated threshold (e.g. overlap-rate reduction %, fewer attempts-to-clean-close) qualifying 'measurably' (E2 signal 2 / F1 subjective-term check)
findings.finding: The verdict AC asks whether the exclusion list 'measurably' beats plain resume, but the plan states no decision threshold — with only 2 tickets and one run per arm there is no defined effect size or margin that constitutes 'measurably beat', leaving the go/no-go call to executor judgment.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — 'does the exclusion list measurably beat plain cache-seeded resume?'
scenarios: Treatment shows a 5% overlap reduction on one ticket and a wash on the other; two reviewers reach opposite go/no-go conclusions because 'measurably' was never operationalized.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Patch verify_step_floor at BOTH bound sites (rebar.llm.completion.verify_step_floor AND the import-time binding used by completion_banking.py:242) so the reduced budget applies uniformly to the primary sizing (completion.py:237) and the recovery-pool sizing (plan_recovery_pool).
evidence: Plan: 'monkeypatches verify_step_floor itself (src/rebar/llm/completion.py:76) ... for every arm and attempt uniformly'
completion_banking.py:38 `from rebar.llm.completion import verify_step_floor` (import-time bound name)
completion_banking.py:242 `floor = verify_step_floor(criteria_count, verify_cfg, direct_children=direct_children)` sizes the recovery pool
completion.py:237 replace(cfg, max_iterations=step_floor) uses the module-local name (would be patched)
findings.finding: The step-floor forcing monkeypatch may not apply uniformly: the plan patches only rebar.llm.completion.verify_step_floor (completion.py:76), but completion_banking.py binds the name at import time (`from rebar.llm.completion import verify_step_floor`, line 38) and uses that bound reference in plan_recovery_pool (line 242) to size the successor/recovery budget pool. Patching the completion module attribute will not reach the banking module's already-bound name, so the resume arms' recovery budgets could still be computed from the full (un-reduced) floor.
scenarios: Resume arms run with a full-size recovery budget while attempt 1 runs reduced, breaking the uniform-budget requirement and confounding steps-to-verdict metrics
findings.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch `rebar.llm.workflow.completion_banking.verify_step_floor` in addition to `rebar.llm.completion.verify_step_floor`, or patch both to the same stub, so both the primary max_iterations floor and the successor recovery-pool budget reflect the reduced value.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the argument-match rule for 're-search overlap' (exact normalized-argument equality on {path, grep-pattern, dir}, and how offsets/superset listings are treated) so the overlap rate is computed identically across arms.
evidence: 're-search overlap rate per attempt (tool calls repeating any earlier attempt's arguments, same arm)'
Step 4 derives searched-set from 'paths read, patterns tried' but the overlap comparison's equality rule is unstated (E2 signal 2: implicit criterion for a derived metric)
findings.finding: The 're-search overlap rate' metric names 'tool calls repeating any earlier attempt's arguments' but does not define the argument-match semantics: whether a repeat requires exact-string equality of arguments, whether grep patterns/paths are normalized, and whether reading the same file at a different offset or a superset dir-listing counts as a repeat.
findings.location: Step 6 (Metrics table) — 're-search overlap rate per attempt'
scenarios: Two executors compute divergent overlap rates because one treats a re-grep with a broadened pattern as a repeat and the other does not, making the A-vs-B comparison non-reproducible.
findings.suggested_fix: State: 'a tool call is a repeat iff its normalized (tool, primary-argument) tuple — file path for reads, canonicalized regex for greps, dir for listings — exactly matches a call in any earlier attempt of the same arm; offset/limit differences do not count as distinct.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the exact prompt-assembly seam the exclusion summary is injected into (primary verify prompt / seeded_context_block vs. successor_system_prompt/successor_instructions) consistent with whichever resume path the arms actually exercise.
evidence: Plan step 5B: 'an exclusion summary injected into the verifier prompt'
completion_verdict_cache.py:297 seeded_context_block emits 'Already credited — do not re-verify' — a pre-existing skip directive
completion_recovery.py:270 successor_system_prompt, :309 successor_instructions — the successor prompt seam
findings.finding: The exclusion-summary injection point is under-specified. Step 5B says the summary is 'injected into the verifier prompt' but there are two distinct prompt-assembly seams — the primary verify prompt (which already appends seeded_context_block, an 'Already credited — do not re-verify' directive at completion_verdict_cache.py:297) and the successor path's successor_system_prompt/successor_instructions (completion_recovery.py:270,309). The plan should name which seam receives the exclusion list, and note that seeded_context_block is a pre-existing structurally-similar mechanism the treatment builds on.
findings.location: Protocol step 2 & step 5B (transcript capture / treatment injection)
scenarios: Harness injects the exclusion list at a seam that the actual resume path does not use, so the treatment arm's summary never reaches the model

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the concrete structure of the injected exclusion summary (per-criterion layout, path-vs-pattern labeling, and where it is inserted into the verifier prompt), since it is the experiment's independent variable.
evidence: Step 5B: 'an exclusion summary injected into the verifier prompt, regenerated after each attempt'
Step 4: 'a compact exclusion summary (<=1500 chars)' derived from 'per-criterion searched-set (paths read, patterns tried)'
Why: format shown only as '"already searched, found nothing: ..."'
ABSENCE: no concrete format spec (sectioning, path-vs-pattern labeling, prompt insertion point) for the LLM-consumed treatment string
findings.finding: The exclusion summary injected into the verifier prompt (the experimental treatment) has no defined structure/shape — only a semantic gloss ('already searched, found nothing: ...') and a <=1500-char cap. How per-criterion searched-sets are laid out, how read-paths are distinguished from grep-patterns, and where in the prompt the summary is placed are unspecified.
scenarios: Harness author must invent the injected-string format ad hoc, making the A/B contrast non-reproducible and the treatment's effect hard to attribute

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete symbol/file:line of the verifier tool-executor seam that step 2 monkeypatches for argument-level transcript capture, as steps 1 and 3 do for their seams.
evidence: Plan: 'wrap the verifier's tool executor in-harness (monkeypatch at the workflow seam) to log every tool call with full arguments'
Steps 1 and 3 cite exact seams (completion_verdict_cache.py:59, completion.py:76 and :237) but step 2 gives only 'the workflow seam'
search_files for 'tool_executor' and 'def execute_tool' under src/rebar/llm(/workflow) returned (no matches)
findings.finding: Step 2's tool-call transcript capture names no concrete monkeypatch target ('wrap the verifier's tool executor in-harness (monkeypatch at the workflow seam)'), unlike steps 1 and 3 which cite exact file:line seams (cache_dir at completion_verdict_cache.py:59, verify_step_floor at completion.py:76). Searches for an obvious executor symbol (tool_executor, def execute_tool) under src/rebar/llm/workflow returned no matches, so the seam the harness depends on for its core deliverable (argument-level transcripts) is unidentified.
scenarios: Harness author must locate the tool-dispatch seam by hand; if the actual seam differs from an assumed one, transcript capture (the PoC's blocking prerequisite) fails or captures incomplete arguments

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item 'Harness exists in the experiment worktree (throwaway; NOT pushed to Gerrit; no s' cites operational evidence (merge_gate) that lives outside the codebase but is not tagged [operator-attested]; prefix the checkbox text with [operator-attested] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Note the pink-elephant risk of naming excluded paths in a negation frame and either specify guarding phrasing or add a per-attempt sanity check that arm B does not re-search the enumerated paths more than arm A.
evidence: Why: exclusion framed as '"already searched, found nothing: ..."'
Verdict AC: 'does the exclusion list measurably beat plain cache-seeded resume?'
ABSENCE: no note on prompt phrasing that mitigates the pink-elephant effect, nor a check that the treatment arm actually reduces (not increases) re-search of the named paths
findings.finding: The exclusion summary uses a negation framing that names the excluded paths/patterns ('already searched, found nothing: <paths>'), a pink-elephant risk: enumerating locations to avoid can attract the model to re-search them, and the plan neither guards the phrasing nor validates that the model honors the exclusion. Since 'does the exclusion list measurably beat plain cache-seeded resume?' is the verdict question, an antipattern in the injected text could invert the measured effect.
scenarios: The treatment prompt lists paths under a 'found nothing' header and the verifier re-reads exactly those paths, inflating overlap in arm B

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the fallback when forced attempt 1 does not fail insufficiency-only (e.g., lower the budget further or select a larger-surface ticket) so the resume arms start from the intended precondition.
evidence: Step 3: 'attempt 1 then FAILs insufficiency-only with a partial bank; keep the transcript'
ABSENCE: no branch for 'attempt 1 did not fail insufficiency-only' (passed, or failed for another reason)
findings.finding: No fallback is specified for the case where forced attempt 1 does NOT fail insufficiency-only — e.g., it PASSes within the reduced budget or fails for a non-insufficiency reason. The entire resume-loop experiment (steps 5-6) presupposes an insufficiency-only fail with a partial bank.
scenarios: A reduced budget of 12-20 steps still lets a small-surface criterion PASS, or the run fails on a non-insufficiency error, leaving no partial bank to resume from

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the control arm reproduces the actual locust resume path (cache-seed into the bank via seed_bank_from_cache PLUS the in-run banked-successor loop _run_successors), and state explicitly whether a 'resume attempt' is a fresh verify_completion invocation or the in-run successor loop.
evidence: Plan: 'the cache accrues within the arm across attempts (that accrual IS the resume mechanism)'
Plan: '(A) CONTROL — plain re-runs, cache-seeded only (locust behavior)'
completion_recovery.py:152 seed_bank_from_cache seeds the bank at run start
completion_recovery.py:242 _run_successors runs a banked-successor loop over the unverified remainder within one run
findings.finding: The plan's model of the resume mechanism may not match production. It states the verdict cache 'accrues within the arm across attempts (that accrual IS the resume mechanism)' and defines the control as 'plain re-runs, cache-seeded only'. But completion_recovery.py shows production resume is an in-run flow: seed_bank_from_cache (line 152) seeds cached PASSes into the CriterionBank at run start, then a banked-successor loop (_run_successors, line 242) re-plans over the unverified remainder WITHIN a single verify invocation. Accrual across a single run is the bank, and each re-run also carries the in-run successor loop. Treating the control as bare cache-seeded re-runs risks not reproducing the locust behavior the experiment is compared against.
scenarios: Control arm under-represents production resume (which includes in-run banked successors), so the A/B comparison measures the exclusion list against a weaker-than-real baseline

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the truncation/selection rule when a criterion's frontier exceeds the 1500-char cap (e.g., drop-order priority) so the treatment summary is deterministic.
evidence: Step 4: 'derive per-criterion searched-set (paths read, patterns tried) and a compact exclusion summary (<=1500 chars)'
ABSENCE: no rule for reducing an over-cap frontier to <=1500 chars
findings.finding: No truncation/selection policy is specified for when a criterion's derived frontier exceeds the 1500-char exclusion-summary cap — which searched paths/patterns are dropped, and by what priority, is undefined.
scenarios: A large-surface ticket (near 8000-char description, many ACs) produces a frontier larger than 1500 chars for some criterion
